isolation: Every assertion in this run is anchored to an entity created fresh by this run (books book-18..book-21 created via the staff UI/API with a run-unique title prefix 'val-1791078147', a new order placed against book-18, a new shipping address '...42 Validation Way, Testopolis', and a new stock reservation order-validation-1791078352), never against pre-existing seeded catalog rows or entities left over from a prior validation run. The one exception is the profile-creation scenario, where Marco's account already had a profile from a prior run; test-shopper-two (Elena) was genuinely blank ('first time') and was used in Marco's place to exercise that specific precondition honestly, noted on that scenario. Cross-shopper isolation scenarios used test-shopper (Marco) and test-shopper-two (Elena) as two distinct accounts: before each isolation assertion, Elena's cart/orders/addresses/notifications were confirmed empty (or shown to lack the run-unique entity) via the same UI path a real shopper would use.

Marco is signed in as a Shopper
steps.command: signed in via IdP as test-shopper

steps.text: Marco tries to view every current reservation
steps.command: /staff/inventory route guard redirects Marco to /forbidden; no reservations view reachable, so attempted against the webapp's own API: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <marco>" http://development-default.openchoreoapis.localhost:19080/p3-1004b-inventory-service-http/reservations

steps.text: Marco is refused
steps.command: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <marco>" .../reservations  vs.  curl -i .../reservations (no Authorization header at all)
steps.observed: both requests return byte-identical 401 responses (same status, same content-length:58, same body {"error":"Unauthorized","message":"Authentication failed"}). Marco's token is independently confirmed live in the same run (it created the reservation above and reads/writes cart, orders, addresses, profile around this same timestamp), so this is not a dead-token false negative -- but the gateway's 401 is, by design, indistinguishable between 'no token' and 'valid token missing a scope'. Whether Marco was refused BY THE RULE (vs. by some unrelated gateway condition) cannot be settled from this evidence. Unchanged since the prior validation run.

evidence.snapshot: GET .../reservations with Marco's valid-but-unscoped bearer token -> HTTP/1.1 401, content-length 58, body {"error":"Unauthorized","message":"Authentication failed"}. The same GET with no Authorization header at all -> identical HTTP/1.1 401, identical content-length 58, identical body. The gateway gives no signal distinguishing a correctly-enforced missing-scope refusal from an unauthenticated request never reaching the app.
